title: test-0053-SCI-PHY-FORCEPRESSURE
passage: Forces are interactions between objects that can change an object's state of motion or shape. A common misunderstanding is that forces are only exerted by living things, but inanimate objects like walls or tables also exert forces. For instance, when a book rests on a table, gravity pulls it down, while the table pushes it upward with an equal force, keeping it stationary. Forces are not 'contained' within an object; they only exist during an interaction. Furthermore, forces like magnetism can act over a distance without physical contact. Pressure is defined as the force acting perpendicularly on a unit area. This explains why a sharp needle pierces skin easily compared to a blunt one; the same force applied over a smaller area creates much higher pressure. Fluids, including air and liquids, also exert pressure. Atmospheric pressure exists because air has weight, and it acts in all directions, not just downwards. Even when an object is not moving, like a heavy box on the floor, friction can act on it to prevent sliding. Understanding these principles helps us see that forces and pressure are fundamental to how the physical world operates, regardless of whether an object is in motion or at rest.
summary: Forces are when objects move or change shape. Understanding these principles helps us see that forces and pressure are fundamental to how the physical world operates, regardless of whether an object is in motion or at rest.
